visual_description: White marble tower ~45m. Tall rectangular top block with turquoise tile panel, on a wide inverted-Y/Y-shaped base: a huge pointed (ogive) central arch flanked by two sloping faceted wings, the whole base a wide trapezoid with fine vertical ribbing. Turquoise tilework in the arch soffit. Sits on a plaza with a reflecting pool.

Tall rectangular red-brick tower (about 3 stacked tiers) with a round clock face on the upper section, a small octagonal/domed crown on top with a flag, slender pilasters and arched windows, set within the ochre-brick Municipality palace building with lower wings.

Long low brick/stone bridge with 33 pointed arches in two tiers: an upper arcade of arched openings along the full length, lower row of pier arches over the river; wider pavilion bulges at both ends; ochre sandstone and brick. About 295m long, very elongated horizontal composition.

Terrace platform of grey-gold limestone on the foot of a mountain; Gate of All Nations with winged bull guardians, a grand double stair, and rows of slender fluted columns (some with bull-head capitals) of the Apadana, many broken.

Achaemenid-inspired white-granite monument on a stepped terraced base: a squared tomb block with tall front columns, a stair, and a cuboid body with relief panels, set in a formal garden with a reflecting pool.
Large three-storey facade of tall symmetrical recessed arches in rows (3 levels, ~25 niches), with two minarets on top flanking the facade; sand-coloured adobe/brick, a square plaza in front.

Huge adobe mud-brick citadel on a rise: crenellated walls with many square watchtowers, a tall central citadel (governor's quarter) at the peak, stepped honeycomb of ruined dwellings below; uniform ochre-sand colour.
Tall 72m red-brick tower: a ten-sided fluted body with ten triangular buttresses, a conical brick roof on top, on a mound; two Kufic bands near top (no text drawn). Very slender vertical silhouette.

Massive turquoise-blue double-shell dome (~50m) on an octagonal drum, with 8 slender minarets at the corners (8 minarets); brick body with tall arched portals and arcaded gallery at the dome's base, turquoise tile accents, plain surrounding.
Modern tomb: a tall tower of 12 pillars with a conical roof on a square base (inspired by Gonbad-e Qabus-style tower), set on a platform surrounded by columns, with a garden.
Two large arched iwans carved into a rock cliff face (large and small), semicircular tops, relief figures within, a spring pool below the cliff reflecting the arches; trees alongside.

Sassanid-era brick/stone castle on a hilltop in Khorramabad: a large rectangular mass with 12 round towers/ramparts, walls with crenellated ends, a stone/brick body, squat towers; sits on the hill above the city.
Stepped mud-brick ziggurat of ~4 receding tiers (originally 5), square plan with central stair ramps on the sides, golden ochre brick on a flat plain, partially ruined top.

Sufi shrine ensemble: a main tomb with a blue-tiled conical dome/tower with a fluted cylinder, adjacent arched porch/iwans in brick, lower domed halls, and a courtyard with a gate; blue and turquoise tile accents on brick.

Armenian monastery (St. Thaddeus), black-and-white striped stone church: a rectangular basilica with a polygonal drum and conical roof over the center, a front arched porch, striped black/white stone courses, nestled in a green valley.
Hilltop brick-and-stone castle in forest: a long polygonal wall with ~40 towers/crenellated watchtowers climbing the slope, tall walls, two main gates; surrounded by dense green forest and mist.

Tall railway viaduct (~110m) across a gorge: one main large central arch and several smaller arches at the ends (one source says 1 main + 10 secondary), straight horizontal deck, masonry piers; train track on top. Arch count conflicts between sources.

Safavid brick gatehouse (~17m): a rectangular two-level facade with a tall central pointed portal arch (pishtaq) framed by a rectangular panel, a large tile window above, and flanking wings; calligraphy panel on the portal (no text drawn).

Village of dry-stone houses stacked on a steep slope in ~20 flat-roofed terraces forming a pyramid; each roof serves as the yard of the house above; stone grey-ochre with blue window frames and wooden elements.

Hilltop stone-and-gypsum Qajar-era governor's castle: a rectangular walled compound with corner round towers and a central mass, flat roofs, set on a hill above Ilam city and surrounded by oak forest.
Square/rectangular stone fort with round bastion towers on the corners, thick walls and crenellations, on a low promontory by the sea; red-ochre island rock around.

Row of 2-3 storey flat-roofed coastal houses in cream/ochre with wooden balconies and shutters, small arched windows, a minaret/lighthouse tower at one side, wooden dhows moored on the water in front.
Isolated dark-brown volcanic hill rising from a lake plain, a ruined mud-brick fortress (Ghaleh Kafaran) with stepped walls and crenellations on top; reflected in the water.
Qajar-era garden in Birjand: a central two-storey pavilion with columned porch and symmetrical facade, long axial water pool and channels, tall surrounding walls, trees; sand-coloured.

Qajar-era brick mansion in Bojnord, symmetrical, two floors with a porch on each floor on north and south sides, columned porches with brick and turquoise/yellow tile accents, ~34 rooms, two large halls.

Oldest surviving Persian mosque (8th c.): a courtyard of rounded brick arches on thick short round columns (hypostyle arcades), a tall cylindrical brick minaret on one side; plain unadorned sand-coloured brick.
Large shrine with a golden dome and gold-topped minarets, an iwan with turquoise/blue tilework at the entrance, courtyard walls, golden roof glints; blue and gold palette.
Historic covered Soltani bazaar: long brick-vaulted passage with a row of shallow domes/skylights, pointed arch entrances and arcade shops on both sides, light shafts from roof openings.
Old stone-and-brick bridge over a river on rocks; arch count not verified (search did not return details) and one source places it in Isfahan Province.
Waterfall dropping over a rocky cliff in a forested ravine, a main wide fall with a pool below, surrounded by oak trees and rock walls.

Safavid caravanserai: a large rectangular brick/stone complex with a tall pointed arched gate (pishtaq) at the center, a central courtyard with arcaded rooms in two tiers, low domed roofs; material (brick vs stone) differs between sources.
